newsitem.title: UK: Man Utd shares slip on BkyB deal worries.
newsitem.headline: Man Utd shares slip on BkyB deal worries.

text.p: Shares in English football league champions Manchester United slipped on Friday after news late Thursday that the European Commission may probe the BSkyB's exclusive UK soccer deal, traders said
Manchester United stock was down 19p to 524p mid-morning and has fallen 70p -- 12 percent -- since speculation about a bid for the club was at its height two weeks ago.
"If a probe in any way threatens the BSkyB deal it will have an enormous impact on these clubs because TV money makes up a large part of their revenue now, " said Nomura's Allison Southey.

EU Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said on Thursday he was monitoring a television rights deal between BSkyB and English soccer's Premier league though he had not called for a formal investigation into it.
"The BSkyB was the key thing that crystallised the interest in football stocks, so it is a worry," said Southey
Speculation of a takeover for Manchester United has also faded recently, traders said.
Granada, Whitbread and Mark McCormack's IMG marketing agency were all linked with a bid but solid evidence of an imminent approach for the club has failed to materialise.
